title: `RenderingDevice.texture_clear()` behaves differently between the Vulkan and D3D12 driver, depending on the `DataFormat` of the texture
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: v4.7.dev2, v4.6.1.stable ### System information Godot v4.7.dev2 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT (AMD; 26.2.2) - AMD Ryzen 5 3600 (12 threads) - 31.90 GiB memory ### Issue description Textures created and cleared on the main rendering device are displayed differently between the Vulkan and D3D12 graphics driver, depending on the used `DataFormat` of the texture. In the tested conditions, only `DATA_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM` and `DATA_FORMAT_R8_UNORM` lead to the same outcome with both drivers. ```gdscript extends Node @export var sprite_0 : Sprite2D @export var sprite_1 : Sprite2D @export var sprite_2 : Sprite2D @export var sprite_3 : Sprite2D var texture_0 : Texture2DRD var texture_1 : Texture2DRD var texture_2 : Texture2DRD var texture_3 : Texture2DRD func _ready(): RenderingServer.call_on_render_thread(create_textures) return func create_textures(): var main_rd := RenderingServer.get_rendering_device() var tf := RDTextureFormat.new() tf.format = RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM tf.texture_type = RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_TYPE_2D tf.width = 256 tf.height = 256 tf.usage_bits = (RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_USAGE_SAMPLING_BIT | RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_USAGE_CAN_COPY_TO_BIT) var texture_rid_0 = main_rd.texture_create(tf, RDTextureView.new()) tf.format = RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R32G32B32A32_SFLOAT var texture_rid_1 = main_rd.texture_create(tf, RDTextureView.new()) tf.format = RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R8_UNORM var texture_rid_2 = main_rd.texture_create(tf, RDTextureView.new()) tf.format = RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R32_SFLOAT var texture_rid_3 = main_rd.texture_create(tf, RDTextureView.new()) main_rd.texture_clear(texture_rid_0, Color.HOT_PINK, 0, 1, 0, 1) main_rd.texture_clear(texture_rid_1, Color.HOT_PINK, 0, 1, 0, 1) main_rd.texture_clear(texture_rid_2, Color.HOT_PINK, 0, 1, 0, 1) main_rd.texture_clear(texture_rid_3, Color.HOT_PINK, 0, 1, 0, 1) texture_0 = Texture2DRD.new() texture_1 = Texture2DRD.new() texture_2 = Texture2DRD.new() texture_3 = Texture2DRD.new() texture_0.texture_rd_rid = texture_rid_0 texture_1.texture_rd_rid = texture_rid_1 texture_2.texture_rd_rid = texture_rid_2 texture_3.texture_rd_rid = texture_rid_3 sprite_0.texture = texture_0 sprite_1.texture = texture_1 sprite_2.texture = texture_2 sprite_3.texture = texture_3 return ``` From left to right: `DATA_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM`, `DATA_FORMAT_R32G32B32A32_SFLOAT`, `DATA_FORMAT_R8_UNORM`, `DATA_FORMAT_R32_SFLOAT` Result using the Vulkan driver: Result using the D3D12 driver: ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create and clear textures from code using different DataFormats 2. Display the textures using `Sprite2D` 3. Observe differences based on the current graphics driver (Vulkan or D3D12) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25822884/MRP.zip)
